title: Perfect complexes are the saturated triangulated closure of the ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring. In the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the full subcategory of perfect objects [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] is the smallest strictly full, saturated, triangulated subcategory containing the unit object $A[0]$. Here strictly full means closed under isomorphism, and saturated means closed under direct summands. Equivalently, this is the thick subcategory generated by $A[0]$ [pur9-def-thick]: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, distinguished cones and direct summands.
